args: Analyze the ownership/invariant semantics of xmlAddIDSafe in libxml2/valid.c, especially its existing-ID branch, and all non-streaming callers in libxml2/tree.c. Is the correct root fix to replace an existing xmlID's attr pointer whenever a non-streaming attr is supplied and clear the previous attribute's ID metadata? Explain what should happen for repeated duplicate IDs and streaming-created entries.

The reported ASan crash is a heap-use-after-free in xmlRemoveID at libxml2/valid.c:2528 during partial cleanup in xmlStaticCopyNode. An XML reader streaming entry has xmlID->attr NULL. Entity replacement content has two attributes with duplicate ID value. Later xmlDocCopyNode calls xmlAddIDSafe in non-streaming mode for each copied attr. Existing code reportedly only performs ret->attr = attr inside if (ret->attr != NULL), so when initially NULL it leaves both copied attrs pointing via attr->id to the same xmlID while the xmlID points to none. Cleanup of the first removes/frees the xmlID; cleanup of the second dereferences dangling attr->id. I need confirm intended duplicate-ID behavior and minimal safe patch.
